title: New apartments in Bucharest District 6: where supply concentrates and square meter prices
seoTitle: New apartments Bucharest District 6: prices and areas
description: New apartments in Bucharest District 6: 16 active developers, new square meter at 1,542 euros excluding VAT, and western areas with faster supply turnover.
descriptionLlm: Discover the new apartments offer in Bucharest District 6 on Virtutii Boulevard, premium finishes, and details about [apartment prices](/preturi/).
keywords: apartamente noi bucuresti sector 6, apartamente noi sector 6, pret apartament nou sector 6, apartamente noi militari, blocuri noi drumul taberei
lead: If you are looking for new apartments in Bucharest District 6, the starting figures look like this: 16 active developers, 131 individually tracked apartments, and 116 available on September 12, 2026, the verification date. The square meter monitor, which reads developer websites directly, sets the average for that same day at 1,542 euros per square meter excluding VAT, meaning about 1,866 euros with a 21 percent VAT. We present the market situation below: how many new blocks exist, where supply gathers, what entry prices you face, and what you get with the budget of a two room apartment in Titan. Two things stand out quickly. Supply concentrates in the western part of the district, along Militari and Timisoara Boulevard, while toward Politehnica and Regie the newly published stock has nearly vanished. Sales move slowly as the average absorption rate, sold plus reserved, reaches 8 percent across the entire district.

sections.h2: District 6 has 16 active developers and 116 available new apartments

blocks.x: The monitor tracks 131 individually monitored apartments in the district, of which 116 are available, plus 68 offers by typology. These are current figures, taken on September 12, 2026, coming from a single source, so you should use them as a benchmark with the source and date alongside. At an average absorption rate of 8 percent, new blocks in the district move slowly, giving buyers room for negotiation, especially where apartments wait longer. If you want to expand your comparison to the rest of the city, you can look through the apartments for sale listed right now.

sections.h2: New supply concentrates along axes in the western district

blocks.x: The west gathers volume and movement. Militari-Iuliu Maniu places 91 units on the monitor, of which 76 are available, at an average of 1,488 euros per square meter excluding VAT, while Timisoara-Pacii Boulevard holds 12 units, 10 available, at 1,279 euros. These are also the areas where properties move faster: absorption climbs to 16 percent in Militari and 17 percent on Pacii, compared to a district average of 8 percent.

Toward the center of the district, the story changes. Lujerului-Politehnica-Regie has barely 6 available new published apartments, so you are searching among very few options there. Between the ends, Crangasi-Giulesti-Orsova gathers 74 units, all available, with no published average price, while Drumul Taberei-Ghencea stands with 18 available apartments at 2,022 euros per square meter.

The difference between the most expensive area with a published price and the cheapest reaches 1.6 times: 2,022 euros versus 1,279 euros per square meter. For a whole apartment, this difference shows directly in the down payment and monthly installment. It makes sense to glance at apartment prices in the rest of the city before setting your budget.

sections.h2: Published entry prices start below 80,000 euros

blocks.x: At the lower end of the grid, on the verification date, Rotar Park Residence and Panorama City appear, both on the Militari-Iuliu Maniu axis. Rotar publishes entries starting from 72,727 euros excluding VAT, meaning 1,777 euros per square meter, while Panorama City starts from 75,000 euros excluding VAT, at 1,807 euros per square meter. Neofort 49 Militari follows, starting from 77,800 euros, and Yola 71 from 79,900 euros. At the opposite pole, Noble Piatra Craiului, in the Lujerului-Politehnica-Regie area, publishes prices starting from 150,900 euros.

Add the standard 21 percent VAT, valid for homes starting August 1, 2025, and the math shifts: the Rotar entry reaches about 88,000 euros, and the Panorama entry about 90,750. The starting price of a project is not the final invoice, but the threshold for discussion. These names remain examples published by the monitor on September 12, 2026, and the availability of a specific unit should be verified directly with the developer.

sections.h2: With the budget of a two room apartment in Titan you get around 70 usable square meters in District 6

blocks.x: For comparison, we take Ilioara Residence, our building in Titan-Dristor, District 3: ground floor plus eight storeys, 35 apartments, 0 percent commission for the buyer. A two room apartment there starts from 107,500 euros excluding VAT and goes up to 136,500 euros excluding VAT, while a three room apartment starts from 151,000 euros plus VAT. Relative to the District 6 average of 1,542 euros per square meter excluding VAT, a budget of 107,500 euros buys you around 70 usable square meters.

Conversely, a two room apartment of 50 usable square meters, the usual size in a new building, comes out at the district average around 77,100 euros excluding VAT, meaning about 93,000 euros with 21 percent VAT. At 55 usable square meters, the calculation climbs toward 103,000 euros with VAT. Our calculation relies on stated premises: the average of 1,542 euros excluding VAT from September 12, 2026, and the Titan price grid, so you should rerun it whenever prices change. Here is also where you see what formulas starting "from" leave off the invoice: at the Titan building, a single parking space costs 20,000 euros plus VAT, and a double one 25,000 euros plus VAT.

sections.h2: New construction costs more than old, and in Drumul Taberei the jump reaches 18 percent

blocks.x: An analysis by broker credite.cc, published on April 30, 2026, compares prices across District 6 areas, with old and new separated. In Militari, old properties trade between 1,500 and 1,750 euros per square meter, and new construction between 1,750 and 2,100. In Crangasi, the grid climbs from 1,500-1,750 to 1,800-2,150. Drumul Taberei shows the jump most clearly: 1,700-1,950 for old blocks and 1,950-2,350 for new blocks, meaning 18 percent higher, in the table example, 2,150 versus 1,825. Politehnica leads the upper district, with 2,100-2,400 for old and 2,400-2,800 for new, above the city average of approximately 2,000 euros per square meter.

The same analysis discusses trends, to be taken as an estimate from April 2026: an average growth of 3 to 5 percent citywide and 6 to 9 percent in areas with new subway stations. Drumul Taberei enters the M5 subway line and appears in the broker report at the top of the city's price-to-quality ratio.

sections.h2: The appraiser gives an overall District 6 average of 1,670 euros per square meter

blocks.x: This figure includes mixed old and new stock, acting as a general neighborhood benchmark, separate from the new building prices mentioned above. The pretimobil appraiser puts District 6 overall at 1,670 euros per square meter, while sought-after areas remain Politehnica, Grozavesti-Regie, Drumul Taberei, Lujerului, and Uverturii. The neighborhood value map looks like this: Politehnica, Grozavesti, Drumul Taberei, and Lujerului in the prime tier, Virtutii, Crangasi, Gorjului, and Pacii in the middle tier, and Giulesti, Ghencea, and Militari Residence in the accessible tier.

As a city reference, the aggregator hartapreturilor gives a median of 1,851 euros per square meter in September 2026, drawn from 716 active listings across all of Bucharest. District 6 remains below the city average, while new blocks in sought-after areas exceed the district average.

faq.q: Do new apartments in Militari move fast?
faq.a: Faster than the district average. Militari-Iuliu Maniu shows an absorption rate of 16 percent on September 12, 2026, and Timisoara-Pacii Boulevard 17 percent, compared to a district average of 8 percent.

faq.q: Can you buy a new apartment with under 90,000 euros?
faq.a: Yes, on paper, with two caveats. Entries published on the verification date start from 72,727 euros excluding VAT at Rotar Park Residence and from 75,000 euros excluding VAT at Panorama City, both on the Militari-Iuliu Maniu axis; with 21 percent VAT, the first rises to about 88,000 euros, and the second to about 90,750, so the second already crosses the threshold. Above all, you check three things: whether the unit at the entry price still exists, what the price includes, because parking is paid separately, with an example of 20,000 euros plus VAT at the Titan building, and what finishes cost beyond the basic version. Prices starting "from" open the discussion, and you confirm availability with the developer.

faq.q: What budget do I need for a two room apartment of 50 usable square meters?
faq.a: At the district average of 1,542 euros per square meter excluding VAT, the calculation yields around 77,100 euros excluding VAT, meaning about 93,000 euros with VAT. To this sum, you add parking and potential finish upgrades. As an entry example into the payment scheme, the Titan building developer requests a minimum down payment of 30 percent of the price and a 2,000 euros plus VAT reservation fee; for other developers the grid differs, so you should check it beforehand. You usually cover the difference through a mortgage loan, and you rerun the math whenever prices change.
